findings.text: Exposes BUILD_BUG_ON as a compile time assertion facility that forwards to BUILD_BUG_ON_MSG with a default diagnostic tied to the tested condition.

Provides virt_to_fix translating a normal virtual address into a fixed mapping index while requiring the input to remain inside the range bounded by FIXADDR_START and FIXADDR_TOP and delegating conversion to __virt_to_fix with a fatal check through BUG_ON on violation.

Defines FIXMAP_PAGE_NORMAL alongside FIXMAP_PAGE_RO alongside FIXMAP_PAGE_NOCACHE alongside FIXMAP_PAGE_IO alongside FIXMAP_PAGE_CLEAR as standard fixed mapping protections for normal and read only and non cached and device personalities plus a cleared no permission value equated to the PAGE_KERNEL family and to __pgprot for the cleared case.

Offers set_fixmap with clear_fixmap with __set_fixmap_offset with set_fixmap_offset with set_fixmap_nocache with set_fixmap_offset_nocache with set_fixmap_io for installing or removing fixed entries with normal or non cached or device protections including offset returning variants that account for the sub page portion of the supplied physical location.

Supplies get_order determining the allocation order whose page count covers a requested byte size relative to PAGE_SHIFT and BITS_PER_LONG with dedicated treatment for compile time known inputs including zero and sub page sizes and word size dependent bit scan selection otherwise.
Describes irq_cpustat_t as a cache aligned per processor interrupt record holding __softirq_pending as a pending mask and optionally __nmi_count when ARCH_WANTS_NMI_IRQSTAT is selected.
Provides ack_bad_irq as a diagnostic sink for an unexpected vector identified by irq that emits a report at KERN_CRIT severity naming the vector.

Exposes huge_pte_write with huge_pte_dirty with huge_pte_none with huge_pte_uffd as queries on huge entries for writability and dirtiness and emptiness and user fault state forwarded to ordinary table notions.

Exposes huge_pte_mkwrite with huge_pte_wrprotect with huge_pte_mkdirty with huge_pte_modify with huge_pte_mkuffd with huge_pte_clear_uffd as transformations on huge entries adjusting writability and dirtiness and protections and user fault state.

Exposes huge_pte_clear with set_huge_pte_at with huge_ptep_get_and_clear with huge_ptep_clear_flush with huge_ptep_set_wrprotect with huge_ptep_set_access_flags with huge_ptep_get for installing and clearing and retrieving and flushing huge entries with address space and address context delegated to ordinary table primitives.
Reports gigantic_page_runtime_supported from IS_ENABLED applied to CONFIG_ARCH_HAS_GIGANTIC_PAGE so support follows the architecture capability option.
Establishes s8 with u8 with s16 with u16 with s32 with u32 with s64 with u64 as fixed width signed and unsigned aliases for eight and sixteen and thirty two and sixty four bit widths.

Defines S8_C with U8_C with S16_C with U16_C with S32_C with U32_C with S64_C with U64_C in two personalities where one decorates unsigned and wide literals with language suffixes and the other leaves every literal unchanged.

Specifies __io_br with __io_ar with __io_bw with __io_aw with __io_pbw with __io_paw with __io_pbr with __io_par as ordering primitives built on barrier with rmb with wmb with mmiowb_set_pending where acquire and release each have two personalities selecting full memory ordering or compiler only ordering and paged variants reuse the base notions with a pending flush for posted writes.

Provides rwmmio_tracepoint_enabled with log_write_mmio with log_post_write_mmio with log_read_mmio with log_post_read_mmio as tracing hooks carrying width with address with caller context where the enabled personality queries tracepoint state and the disabled personality always reports inactive with silent no operation hooks.

Offers __raw_readb with __raw_readw with __raw_readl with __raw_readq with __raw_writeb with __raw_writew with __raw_writel with __raw_writeq as unordered native width device loads and stores on volatile mapped addresses each paired with a self definition marker for architecture override detection.

Offers readb with readw with readl with readq as ordered little endian device loads with surrounding acquire style ordering and optional pre and post tracing converting through __le16_to_cpu with __le32_to_cpu with __le64_to_cpu.

Offers writeb with writew with writel with writeq as ordered little endian device stores with surrounding release style ordering and optional pre and post tracing converting through cpu_to_le16 with __cpu_to_le32 with __cpu_to_le64.

Offers readb_relaxed with readw_relaxed with readl_relaxed with readq_relaxed with writeb_relaxed with writew_relaxed with writel_relaxed with writeq_relaxed as relaxed device loads and stores preserving little endian conversion with optional tracing while omitting surrounding ordering.

Offers readsb with readsw with readsl with readsq with writesb with writesw with writesl with writesq as repeated block transfers between one device location and a memory buffer for a caller supplied element count with no effect when the count is zero using the matching raw width primitive.
States PCI_IOBASE as the zero based port window origin and IO_SPACE_LIMIT as the sixty four kilobyte minus one ceiling for port offsets.

Provides _inb with _inw with _inl with _outb with _outw with _outl as port loads and stores offset from the port base with paged ordering and little endian conversion where public inb with inw with inl with outb with outw with outl forward to the underscore forms each paired with a self definition marker.

Requires __le16_to_cpu with __le32_to_cpu with __le64_to_cpu with __cpu_to_le32 with __cpu_to_le64 to swap byte order through __swab16 with __swab32 with __swab64 on big endian builds while acting as identity casts on little endian builds for both load and store directions.

Uses __ASM_GENERIC_GETORDER_H with __ASM_GENERIC_HARDIRQ_H with _ASM_GENERIC_HUGETLB_H with __ASM_GENERIC_HW_IRQ_H with _ASM_GENERIC_INT_LL64_H with __ASM_GENERIC_IO_H as single inclusion guards for the respective generic headers.

Out of range input to virt_to_fix ends in a fatal bug check and ack_bad_irq denotes an unexpected vector path at critical severity while raw and port accessors require caller provided mapped volatile addresses with correct width alignment and port bounds observance.
